Based on the review of the problem and the peer responses, all models unanimously and correctly identify the core economic principle at play: marginal analysis. 

A rational consumer maximizes their net satisfaction (utility) by continuing an activity as long as the additional benefit of the next unit exceeds its additional cost ($MB > MC$). They stop consuming right at the point where the additional benefit of the next unit equals its additional cost ($MB = MC$). Consuming beyond this point would mean that the cost of the next cookie outweighs the benefit, thereby decreasing total net utility. 

The peer responses clearly elaborate on why option (B) is the correct choice and why options (A), (C), and (D) are incorrect. No changes to the reasoning are necessary.

Final answer: B
